edges.description: Loss of enhancer-promoter contact is proposed to prevent ZRS-driven SHH transcription in the limb bud. This step is inferred. SHH expression in the embryonic limb bud has not been measured for the human allele; the only human measurement is in EBV-transformed lymphoblastoid cells, where SHH mRNA was low overall and lower in proband than wild-type cells. The orthologous mouse deletion leaves Shh expression unchanged because mouse CTCF architecture differs. Mouse data cut both ways: deleting CTCF sites around the ZRS reduced limb Shh by about half with no limb phenotype, whereas an inversion that disrupted ZRS-Shh contact abolished ZPA Shh and truncated the limb. A partial contact defect may therefore not be enough, and how completely the human deletion silences limb SHH is unknown.

nodes.description: The common Brazilian founder allele, found homozygous in all five families studied by Ianakiev et al. Whole-genome sequencing of one proband refined it to a 12 kb deletion surrounding LMBR1 exon 4. At the RNA level it produces an LMBR1 transcript lacking exon 4 with a downstream premature stop codon. It removes three CTCF sites that tether the ZRS to the SHH promoter; the ZRS itself is not deleted and carried no rare variant in the sequenced proband.

nodes.description: Limb-specific loss of SHH expression from the zone of polarizing activity, with SHH expression elsewhere unaffected (hence modular loss of expression). Direct support comes from mouse: deleting the ZRS abolishes limb-bud Shh expression and truncates the limb distal to the stylopod-zeugopod junction. Unlike the patterning conformers of the module, the consequence here is failure of distal outgrowth rather than altered digit number or identity.
